newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LEMIEUX REDUCED TO TEARS IN POSSIBLE MONTREAL FAREWELL.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LEMIEUX REDUCED TO TEARS IN POSSIBLE MONTREAL FAREWELL.

text.p: His Penguins lost but Pittsburgh superstar Mario Lemieux will never forget what was likely his last regular-season game in his native Montreal.

Lemieux scored twice Wednesday in the 8-5 defeat by the Canadiens, on a night in which the burly centre was reduced to fighting back tears by a trio of prolonged standing ovations from the appreciative Molson Centre crowd.

"It's probably the first time in my life an ovation got to me," Lemieux said of the warm reception he received from Montreal fans after he scored his first goal of the game with 4:01 left in the third period.

"It was so loud and for so long. It's a good thing the puck dropped to go on with the game," said Lemieux, who has said he will retire at the end of this season, concluding 13 brilliant years in the NHL.

Lemieux, who also had three assists, picked up his second goal and 46th of the season in the final minute, and when the final siren sounded, he received his third standing ovation as Montreal players came off the bench to congratulate him.
"To me, it's tear-jerking stuff," Penguins coach Craig Patrick said. "I thought the Montreal fans were excellent and Mario deserved it. I thought it was great."

Canadiens captain Vincent Damphousse, who picked up his 26th goal in the third period, said: "It was a great scenario for the fans. We won the game and Mario Lemieux scored five points in his last game at the Molson Centre."
Damphousse, an admitted Lemieux fan, added: "I congratulated him and asked him for his stick, but he wanted it for himself so he's going to send me one."
The Canadiens jumped all over rookie goaltender Patrick Lalime in the first period, scoring on their first three shots and taking a 4-0 lead before Pittsburgh got off its first shot on goal.
Stephane Richer scored two of Montreal's five first-period goals. Mark Recchi also scored twice for the Canadiens.
In Detroit, Darren McCarty scored 39 seconds into overtime as the Red Wings rallied from a two-goal third-period deficit to beat the Colorado Avalanche 6-5 in a fight-filled contest.

Bad blood left over from last year's Western Conference finals led to 18 major penalties for fighting -- including one each to goaltenders Patrick Roy of Colorado and Mike Vernon of Detroit -- and 144 penalty minutes.
Martin Lapointe and Brendan Shanahan scored 36 seconds apart midway through the third period to tie the game before Shanahan set up McCarty's game-winner in overtime.
Valeri Kamensky recorded his third career hat trick for the Avalanche, who were outshot by a wide 47-19 margin.
Vernon picked up his 300th career win despite giving up five goals on just 19 shots.
In Chicago, Denis Savard snapped a tie with 8:01 left and Tony Amonte scored twice in the third period to lift the Blackhawks to a 5-3 victory over the Washington Capitals.

Steve Konowalchuk scored two first-period goals for Washington and Sergei Gonchar gave the Capitals a 3-2 lead 4:30 into the third period. But Amonte tied the game with his 38th goal of the season and added an insurance tally 1:43 after Savard's game winner.
Eric Daze and Ethan Moreau also scored for Chicago, which moved past St Louis into a seventh-place tie with Calgary in the Western Conference playoff race.
In Buffalo, defenceman Bryan Berard scored off a rebound one minute into overtime to lift the New York Islanders to a 3-2 victory over the Sabres.

Bryan McCabe put a wrist shot on net from the high slot and goaltender Steve Shields made the save. But Berard sped between two defenders and put the rebound between the netminder's pads for the game winner.
Dan Plante and Niklas Andersson also scored for New York and Tommy Salo made 25 saves for the Isles. Brad May and Miroslav Satan scored the Buffalo goals.
In San Jose, Felix Potvin turned aside 40 shots and Mats Sundin scored a short-handed goal early in the second period as the Toronto Maple Leafs edged the Sharks 2-1.
Brandon Convery also scored for Toronto, which mathematically eliminated the Sharks from playoff contention.
Darren Turcotte had the lone San Jose goal, spoiling Potvin's shutout bid with one minute left in the second period.
In Vancouver, Jyrki Lumme, Martin Gelinas, Donald Brashear and Lonny Bohonos each had a goal and an assist as the Canucks skated to a 5-3 win over the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim.
Brian Bellows scored two of Anaheim's three powerplay goals as the Ducks grabbed an early 2-1 lead before surrendering four unanswered goals.
Alexander Mogilny scored the other goal for the Canucks, his 29th of the season.
